Compare the empirical and the model-based thresholds

Source: R/compare_thresholds.R
compare_thresholds.Rd

Puts side by side, for each site x species, the threshold from the reviewed clips (suggest_thresholds()) and the ones from the calibration model (calibrated_thresholds()). The first needs no model but needs a random sample and many clips per cell; the second reaches cells with few clips, through partial pooling, but rests on the form of the model.

Usage

compare_thresholds(
  validation,
  fit,
  scored = NULL,
  target_p = 0.95,
  target_precision = 0.9,
  min_n = 15,
  tolerance = 0.05,
  quality = NULL,
  weighted = NULL,
  sustained = FALSE,
  min_confidence = 0.1,
  grid_step = 0.01,
  lower_prob = 0.05
)

Arguments

validation

Reviewed clips, as for suggest_thresholds(). For random_detections clips, the empirical threshold uses the weighted precision.

fit

Model returned by fit_calibration().

scored

Table returned by score_detections(). Needed for thr_model_precision, model_precision_at_empirical and flag.

target_p

Target of the "probability" rule.

target_precision

Target precision of the empirical threshold and of the "precision" rule.

min_n

Passed to suggest_thresholds().

tolerance

Largest difference between thr_empirical and thr_model_precision, in score units, for "agree".

quality

Optional table of calibration_quality(), joined by the columns site and species that it has.

weighted, sustained

Passed to suggest_thresholds().

min_confidence

Detections below this confidence are not scored.

grid_step

Models fitted with engine = "brms": step of the grid of scores on which the posterior is computed.

With a model fitted with engine = "brms", the posterior of P(TP) is computed once on a grid of scores (step grid_step) for each site x species and assigned to the detections by their score rounded to the grid, so that the cost does not depend on the number of detections; the rounding error is small next to the uncertainty of the calibration. Each detection then gets the posterior mean (p_tp), a lower quantile (p_tp_lower) and the posterior probability that P(TP) >= p_min (pr_reliable). detection_history() can use either rule.

lower_prob

Models fitted with engine = "brms": the probability of the lower quantile of the posterior of P(TP) used for threshold_lower.

Value

A tibble with one row per site x species: site, species, thr_empirical, prec_empirical (the precision that chose the cut), n_support, thr_model_precision, thr_p_tp, p_tp_at_threshold, thr_p_tp_lower (with a brms model), model_precision_at_empirical (the expected precision of the model at thr_empirical), max_reviewed, above_reviewed, quality (with quality) and flag: "agree", "disagree", "model_only", "empirical_only" or "none"; NA without scored.

Details

What to compare. The two rules of the model answer different questions. thr_empirical and thr_model_precision both ask what share of the detections kept are true, so their agreement is direct evidence that the calibration fits the data, and flag compares these two. A large difference points to the model (form, missing covariate) or to the sample (few clips, missing weights); check it before using the threshold. The model thresholds require the target at every higher score, and the empirical one by default does not; sustained = TRUE applies the same rule, at the cost described in suggest_thresholds(). thr_p_tp, the score from which a detection is at least target_p likely to be true, is higher for the same target, is the cut on P(TP) of detection_history(), and does not enter flag.

Before using the model. Use a calibration whose candidates were compared by cross-validation and whose calibration_quality() status is "ok" for the species; give that table in quality to carry the status into the output. A model threshold above the highest reviewed score of the cell (above_reviewed) is an extrapolation.

Reuse. Clips used here to set the threshold should not be reused as confirmation data in the occupancy model without saying so.

See also

post_validation(), which writes this table with fit.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- fit_calibration(read_validations(files),
                       calibration_models()$m4_species_x_site)
scored <- score_detections(tables, fit)
compare_thresholds(read_validation_tables(files), fit, scored)
} # }
